title: Phased Traffic Sentinel: safety heuristics for progressive rollouts
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Build a lightweight, runtime 'Phased Traffic Sentinel' service and orchestration rules to govern progressive delivery for model/runtime upgrades. The sentinel will evaluate multi-signal health heuristics (latency p95/p99, error rate, user-facing degradation, token-cost regressions, model-quality regressions from eval sets) during automated ramps and make deterministic 'proceed/hold/rollback' decisions. This ticket covers the minimal MVP: a scoring engine, integration hooks for rollout orchestration, feature flag correlation, and an auto-rollback policy with manual override and audit logging.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel exposes a stable API for rollout orchestration: /evaluate and /decision with documented contract
Sentinel computes a time-decayed health score from at least 4 signals and returns a deterministic decision code
Integration with existing rollout controller to pause or advance ramps at configured checkpoints (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%)
Auto-rollback triggered when decision == ROLLBACK with an auditable event recorded in release logs and Console alert fired
Playbook documented and reachable from Console with manual override and step-down controls
End-to-end test simulating a latency spike causes sentinel to hold and subsequently rollback in the integration test harness
implementation_notes: Create sentinel as a small stateless service backed by rollout-metrics topic (Kafka) and an in-memory sliding window for per-release scoring
Signals: latency p95/p99 (5m window), 5xx rate (1m & 5m), model-quality delta from golden prompt set (continuous eval hooks), cost-per-token delta
Scoring: normalized z-scores per signal, weighted sum with configurable weights per project; weights stored as feature-flag-like config in ConfigService
Decision thresholds: proceed if score >= -0.5, hold if -1.5 < score < -0.5, rollback if score <= -1.5 (default); values tunable per release channel
Expose webhook sink for Console to display live sentinel decisions and attach to rollout timeline
Rollback path uses existing rollout controller API with idempotent cancel + fallback to last-stable model and a rapid drain policy for in-flight requests
Audit log: all sentinel evaluations must emit event with release_id, cohort, traffic_pct, computed_score, contributing_signals (rounded), decision, and operator_id (if manual)
playbook: Phase 1: Canary (5% for 30m) — sentinel evaluates every 1m; require 10 consecutive 'proceed' ticks to advance
Phase 2: Early ramp (20% for 60m) — stricter thresholds for p99 and model-quality; alert on >2x baseline token-cost regression
Phase 3: Broad ramp (50% for 120m) — monitor business KPIs (latency, errors) in parallel; allow manual hold
Phase 4: Full (100%) — mark release as promoted and emit final audit
Auto-rollback: on 'rollback' decision, trigger immediate traffic reversion, create incident stub, and assign SRE on-call via PagerDuty integration
Manual override: operator can force 'proceed' with reason recorded, but sentinel continues to score and will re-assert at next checkpoint

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy signal causes unnecessary rollback — Mitigation: time-decay + require N consecutive failing ticks before rollback
Risk: telemetry gaps during peak load — Mitigation: treat missing minor signals as neutral and only escalate on core signals (p99/5xx/model-quality)
Risk: operator override hides systemic regression — Mitigation: record override and escalate with auto-assigned incident to SRE
Risk: cascading rollbacks across dependent services — Mitigation: add dependency awareness and staggered rollback windows per service
